step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Purolator's serverless package processing pipeline. It consists of an entry API Gateway routing payloads into three distinct processing paths: 1) Package intent metadata sent via an SQS queue to an INGEST Lambda function writing to RDS; 2) Package lifecycle events (pickup, delivery, disruption scans) sent via another SQS queue to an EVENT PROC Lambda function updating RDS; 3) Captured package dimension images stored in an S3 bucket triggering an IMAGE PROC Lambda function which updates RDS with image references.

graph.name: Purolator Package Ingestion and Event Processing Architecture
graph.notes: Architectural overview of Purolator's serverless package handling pipeline capable of processing 5 million package events daily, decoupling ingestion, lifecycle event processing, and package dimension image metadata into RDS.

nodes.name: GATEWAY
nodes.notes: API Gateway fronting incoming traffic from handheld devices, external systems, and facility scanners.

nodes.name: SQS Ingest
nodes.notes: SQS queue buffering incoming package creation intent messages.

nodes.name: SQS Event
nodes.notes: SQS queue buffering status and tracking lifecycle events (pickup, facility scans, delivery status).

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Amazon S3 bucket storing images captured during redimensioning and reweighing scans.

nodes.name: INGEST
nodes.notes: Ingestion Lambda processing package creation declarations.

nodes.name: EVENT PROC
nodes.notes: Event Processing Lambda executing tailored business logic for varied package lifecycle events.

nodes.name: IMAGE PROC
nodes.notes: Image Processing Lambda handling image metadata and creating image links in RDS.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Amazon RDS database acting as the single source of truth for package status and history.

edges.notes: Gateway routes initial package intent metadata JSON into the SQS Ingest queue.
SQS Ingest queue triggers INGEST Lambda.
INGEST Lambda writes initial relational package records into RDS.
Gateway receives lifecycle event updates from driver handhelds and forwards them to SQS Event queue.
SQS Event queue triggers EVENT PROC Lambda.
EVENT PROC Lambda updates package event states in RDS.
Gateway uploads captured package scan images to S3 bucket.
S3 image creation triggers IMAGE PROC Lambda.
IMAGE PROC Lambda writes a reference link to the S3 image into RDS.
